facility_name: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH), Renal Centre
evidence_note: Renal centre manager Hamamatu Haruna says the centre runs round the clock on a standby generator and recorded 1,162 dialysis patients from Jan–Sep 2025, but has too few staff to meet demand. Quote: "We run a morning/evening shift, and we are few."

facility_name: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH)
evidence_note: Under the federal subsidy, the Federal Ministry of Health gave ATBUTH one new machine and consumables. The article gives no total machine count. Quote: "provided a new dialysis machine to support the hospital's efforts"

facility_name: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH)
evidence_note: Session price before and after the federal subsidy began at ATBUTH (January 2025). Quote: "from N40,000 to N12,000 per session"

facility_name: Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (ATBUTH)
evidence_note: World Kidney Day 2026 report. Dialysis at ATBUTH is subsidised to N12,000 and many patients come from neighbouring states, yet one patient still missed a booked session because he could not pay. Quote: "I was booked for dialysis last week but I could not meet the date because of my economic condition."

facility_name: RCCG-donated dialysis centre, Bauchi (presented at ATBUTH; the article does not state the host facility)
evidence_note: The RCCG donated a dialysis centre to Bauchi State with 3 machines, a reverse-osmosis water system and a 30KVA generator. The handover took place at ATBUTH. Quote: "the center in Bauchi has three Dialysis Machines"

The State Executive Council approved buying four dialysis machines for the state specialist hospital, mainly for less-privileged patients. This is an approval, not a confirmed installation. Quote: "four world-class renal dialysis machines"

The governor commissioned dialysis and diagnostic equipment for the state specialist hospital. No machine count is given. Quote: "commissioned strategic, diagnostics and dialysis equipment procured by his administration for the Bauchi Specialist Hospital"

In March 2025, FMC Azare had not started the federal subsidised dialysis programme. A hospital source said no circular and no consumables had arrived. Quote: "had not received any official circular and consumables for the programme"

A list published in August 2026 includes FMC Azare among the subsidised dialysis hospitals. No machine count or working status is given. Quote: "FMC Azare is included among the federal hospitals where eligible patients can access subsidised dialysis"

A peer-reviewed survey of all haemodialysis (HD) units in Borno and Yobe (data collected Jan–Jun 2023 during patients' sessions) found two HD facilities in Borno: UMTH and State Specialist Hospital Maiduguri. Quote: "The study encompassed all HD facilities in the north-eastern states of Borno and Yobe, specifically ... University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital (UMTH), and State Specialist Hospital in Maiduguri"

The CMD said UMTH recently acquired 20 machines after the September 2024 floods damaged parts of the hospital. Subsidised sessions cost N12,000. Working status is not stated. Quote: "he said it recently acquired 20 dialysis machines."

facility_name: University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital (UMTH), Kidney Centre
evidence_note: The kidney centre head reported 21 machines installed as part of N1bn of TETFund-funded equipment. The article does not say they are all dialysis machines or whether they work. Quote: "21 machines for renal transplant and treatment"

The state's free dialysis programme started about 2.5 years before Aug 2022 with 10 machines. Sessions rose from 40 to more than 90 a week. The current machine count is not given. Quote: "started two and half years ago with 10 machines"
The head of internal medicine said rising material costs strain government funding for free sessions. Self-paying patients pay about N40,000 a session. Quote: "inflation in the cost of materials"

The unit in-charge reported more than 12,000 free sessions (Dec 2019–Apr 2024) for 668 patients. He said consumables are now restocked and the main gap is staff. Quote: "our challenge here for now is the need for more staff, particularly Nephrology Nurses."

The same peer-reviewed survey (data from 2023) found two HD facilities in Yobe: YSUTH Damaturu and FMC Nguru. Quote: "The study encompassed all HD facilities in the north-eastern states of Borno and Yobe, specifically Yobe State University Teaching Hospital (YSUTH) in Damaturu, Federal Medical Center in Nguru"

The study links fewer patients at FMC Nguru, despite it being nearer the high-burden Bade LGA, to payment: YSUTH dialysis is free for Yobe indigenes, FMC Nguru's is not. Quote: "it provides free dialysis for Yobe State indigenes, as a state hospital, whereas FMC Nguru, a federal hospital, does not offer such support"

facility_name: Yobe State University Teaching Hospital (YSUTH), Damaturu
evidence_note: The CMD said five newly bought machines and a new water treatment plant bring the unit to 11 functional machines. It runs 600–700 free sessions a month, costing the state about N360m a year. Quote: "bringing the total number of functional dialysis machines at the facility to 11"

facility_name: Modibbo Adama University Teaching Hospital (MAUTH), Yola
evidence_note: A politician donated 200 consumable kits to lower patient costs. The CMD gave the average cost per cycle at MAUTH. No machine count is given. Quote: "an average cycle cost N100,000 in the facility."

The governor inspected the hospital's dialysis machine, which is used without charge to kidney patients. The text refers to one machine but does not give a total. Quote: "being used free of charge to assist kidney patients"

facility_name: Yola Specialist Hospital (Adamawa State Specialist Hospital)
evidence_note: The state set up a dialysis complex at the hospital and offers dialysis at no charge to patients. No machine count is given. Quote: "established a state-of-the-art dialysis complex at the hospital"

Two FTH Gombe nephrologists are named (Dr Alaya Abdulrashid, Dr Abubakar Sadik). The total number is not stated. Quote: "At the Federal Teaching Hospital Gombe, nephrologists say there are signs of progress in the management of the disease."

An FTH Gombe nephrologist names cost as the main barrier to dialysis. The article does not describe the hospital's dialysis unit or machines. Quote: "access to dialysis remains a major challenge for many patients due to the high cost of treatment"

Profile of the governor's health work (undated; page says '3 years ago', so about 2023). It says a dialysis centre built earlier had been left without equipment and has now been equipped. No count is given. Quote: "equipping of the dialysis centre constructed by the past administration but left unequipped"

An old report of a planned purchase of 6 machines, plus a water treatment plant, for the newly built dialysis centre. It is a plan, not an installation. Quote: "The Gombe State Government is to procure six dialysis machines at the cost of N200 million."
The hospital's Internal Medicine page lists a dialysis unit. It gives no machine count and no date beyond the © 2025 footer. Quote: "Dialysis Unit: Haemodialysis services."

Reported while the state specialist hospital was shut. The fallback at FMC Jalingo was limited. Quote: "dialysis services at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Jalingo" are "constrained by malfunctioning machines and limited capacity."

A second outlet on the same January 2026 shutdown reports FMC Jalingo's machines are out of service. The page carries no exact date; it cites a letter dated 8 Jan 2026. Quote: "the dialysis machines at the Federal Medical Centre (FMC), Jalingo, are currently not functioning"

Dialysis stopped when the state shut the whole hospital for renovation and safety reasons (January 2026). Reopening status was not found. Quote: "At the dialysis unit, chronic kidney patients were found stranded and uncertain about their next line of care."

Opinion piece by a Jalingo public-affairs analyst on a local blog (weak source). It says the dialysis section closed around March 2023 because maintenance funds were not released. Quote: "Much needed funds for the maintenance of the equipment in the unit have not been forthcoming."
